title: Italian Game: Giuoco Pianissimo
line: White keeps the center closed and builds up slowly, the way most strong players do today.

steps.text: The Italian Game. Here White chooses the slow way: guard the center first and open it later.
Move the pawn in front of your queen one square. It guards your pawn on e4.

also.c2c3: That is the other main line, which pushes to the center soon. This lesson guards the pawn first.

steps.after: Black's knight comes out and attacks the pawn, which is now guarded.

steps.text: Move the pawn on c2 one square. Later a pawn on d4 will be guarded, and your bishop gets a way back.
Castle. Your king gets away from the center, and the rook comes toward it.
Put your rook on the file of your king pawn. It guards the pawn and backs a later push in the center.
steps.after: Black's edge pawn gets ready to chase your bishop.

steps.text: Step the bishop back before a pawn can chase it. It still aims at the pawn beside the king.
steps.after: Black steps its bishop back for the same reason.

steps.text: Push the pawn on h2 one square. Now no black piece can jump to g4 to hit your knight or the pawn on f2.
steps.hint: The ringed square is where Black would like to put a bishop or a knight.

steps.text: Your knight on b1 has a long trip ahead, by d2 and f1 to g3, near Black's king. Take the first step.
steps.after: Once the knight leaves d2, your other bishop is free to come out.

steps.text: Go on with the knight toward g3. On f1 it also guards your king side.
steps.after: From g3 the knight eyes f5. Both sides build up; the game is decided later, in the middlegame.

summary: Guard the center with pawns, castle, stop the pins, and bring the knight around. The center opens later.
